text: Participants work in teams representing competing platform suppliers. They choose a design approach and buy offered cards. They total card effects, then present a priced offer and explain their choices. Cards stand for equipment, additions, and engineering work. The workshop exercise groups these activities into four broad phases and gives teams six possible missions.

items: Read the assigned mission limits and extra-score rules. You should see: A list of minimums and rewards. If not: Do not assume missions share the same limits.
Set goals and acceptable prices. You should see: A ranked purchase plan. If not: Use market estimates as guides, not caps.
Buy cards through the auction. You should see: A record of cards and actual paid prices. If not: Only the assigned bidder places bids.
Add signed capability effects. You should see: A completed design total. If not: Include negative effects rather than discarding them.
Check compliance, score, and price. You should see: A compliant or noncompliant result with a reason. If not: Fix missing required fields before considering efficiency.
Explain trade-offs, risks, and one process purchase. You should see: A reasoned team presentation. If not: Use evidence, not only a total score.
Mission choices: Protection Priority, Long-Range Survey, People Transport, Mobile Coordination, Equipment Recovery, and Hazard Clearance.

text: The original exercise moves from planning through purchases and design review to a debrief.
Work backward from your mission's minimum capability before spending on attractive extras.
A full inventory is not useful when a required field remains short.
